hbe_stillwater.turn_in_text:
Grey beneath the violet, same as all of them.

I'll hang it up in Tarren Mill. Not as a trophy - as a reminder that this keep had a garrison once, and they lost it, and nobody came.
hbe_stillwater.accept_text:
Durnholde Keep's outer bailey, south-east of the mill. He'll meet you in the open. He thinks of it as his ground and he's not entirely wrong.

The blade is a Durnholde greatsword, kept long after Durnholde fell. Bring it back when you're done. I'd like it to stop being his, and there's no one left alive it can be returned to.

hbe_shamans.turn_in_text:
All of them, and the hollow's drier today than it was yesterday.

I'm not saying that proves anything. I'm saying I've trapped that hollow eleven years and I noticed.

hbe_riflemen.turn_in_text:
All of them, and I got a measuring chain out on that road this morning for the first time since I was posted to this valley.

That's the whole of what I wanted. The fort can wait; the chain couldn't.

hbe_gavin.accept_text:
Centre of the camp at Gavin's Naze, east of the mill. He's quick, he's quiet, and everything he owns opens without a sound - including the ground under his tent, so don't assume he's run if he vanishes.

The ledger will be on him. He doesn't let it out of reach and he never has, which is the single most useful thing about him.

hbe_ironbeard.accept_text:
On the Dun Garok Road, south of the mill. He calls the volley, and you'll hear him before the first shot.

Break him and the rest shoot like men who are frightened, which they are. They're a garrison a very long way from Dun Morogh holding a ridge nobody in Ironforge has thought about in a decade.

hbe_spellbinders.accept_text:
They hold the inner ring of the camp, south-east of the mill, and they bind you in place before they do anything else, so go in fast and go in with someone.

Think about the cost of this. A trained binder could sell his talent in any city still standing. Instead he is stood in a scrap camp in the Hillsbrad hills. Somebody is paying him enough to make that the better offer.

hbe_fissure_north.accept_text:
It's east of the mill, above Gavin's Naze. The Syndicate off the north track first - they have been sitting on that road watching the elves come and go and taking a tithe, and I would like the road clear before I send anybody up it.

Then go up to the mouth itself and look down it. Do not go in. I have had two men offer and I have told both of them no, and I will tell you the same until somebody can tell me what is at the bottom.

dg_mountaineers.accept_text:
Their mountaineers, inside the outer gate of Dun Garok, south of the mill. I need that muster yard quiet long enough to measure it.

And look at the walls while you're in there. No chamfer anywhere, no rubble fill, every corner a true corner. That's not a cave they tidied up. They cut a hold out of a mountain, square, on purpose, and I'd admire it more if I weren't trying to get into it.

dg_brannic.accept_text:
The outer gate of Dun Garok, south of the mill. Bearded axe, a shield scarred in a band at exactly shoulder height, and in fifteen years that axe has only ever swung in one doorway.

He will not come out to you. He has never once come out. You'll have to go to him, in the one place he's had fifteen years to practise standing.

az_prospectors.accept_text:
Below the causeway in Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. You'll hear the chain before you see the lamps - they sound the depth every ten paces and log it.

Alterac sold the pass to the Horde in the Second War and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords scattered into these hills with nothing. This is what nothing looks like when it finds a silver seam it used to own.

az_ashlan.accept_text:
The Face itself, deep in Azurelode Mine south of Southpoint. He carries a mattock with silver worked into the head - a waste of good silver, and he knew it, and he had it made anyway.

I've had his job two years. I'd rather not have it this literally, and I'd rather the men stopped asking me whether he'd have called them back.

dh_varth.accept_text:
Durnholde Keep's gatehouse, south-east of the mill, first thing through the archway.

He'll sound the alarm before he fights - that's his whole function and he's good at it. If you want to get further into that keep than the bailey, the bell has to stop before the shouting starts.

dh_turnkey.accept_text:
The undercroft of Durnholde Keep, south-east of the mill, past the revenants. Thirty keys on a chain and he swings the lot as one.

He kept the cells. In this keep, in those years, there was one prisoner worth keeping and a boy doesn't hold his own keys. I'm aware that's not a military reason. I'm asking anyway.

dh_revenants.accept_text:
Whatever is down there in Durnholde Keep, south-east of the mill. The stair is behind the Lord's Hall.

These were the keep's own garrison - Lordaeron's men, the ones who were here when it fell. They didn't leave. The Syndicate have simply built their camp on top of them and agreed not to go downstairs, which is the most honest thing I know about the Syndicate.

az_grimewick.accept_text:
Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. The pump house is past the sump.

He took a candle down into a gallery full of pump gas, which is how the whole thing started, and the gas is what killed the shift. Thirty years I've blamed the engineers. Turns out it was one kobold and a candle, and he's still holding the candle.

az_kobolds.accept_text:
Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. In through the adit in the rock face, and mind the standing water - it's deeper than the light makes it look and it does not drain anywhere.

That should clear the upper galleries. They'll be back. They're always back. I'd settle for walking my own mine without a torch in one hand and an axe in the other.
